text:
Zoe (Design): dropped a new compact flow for the version-history strip — called 'Focused Confirm' prototype. idea: keep rollback affordance low-ink on timeline items; require an explicit focus/intent before showing a richer confirm panel with context. figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxxx/focused-confirm Marco (PM): short ask: surface whether a revision was a canary and if metrics are incomplete. also want the confirm copy to say exactly what changes and what won't be reverted. Zoe (Design): added a small 'canary (partial metrics)' micro-tag and an expandable one-line explainer. Confirm panel copy draft: "Revert to this revision — routes traffic and switches model version. Runtime flags and infra changes are not reverted." Dev (Eng): implementation notes: avoid loading full diffs in the timeline. preview payload should be tiny; fetch full diff only for the expanded confirm panel. lazy-load with aria-busy while fetching. server exposes two rollback endpoints: safe (gradual) and immediate. Pri (A11y): a11y nits: hover-only reveal is inaccessible. make focused reveal keyboard-activated (Enter/Space). confirm panel must be role=\"dialog\" with aria-modal and a focus trap. screen reader should hear a succinct summary: revision id, author, canary status, and undo window. Zoe (Design): updated interactions: hover shows a thin preview, keyboard focus shows the same, Enter opens the Confirm panel. added aria snippet in notes:
..
Lucy (Support): support note: accidental reverts are a big risk. prefer a two-step confirm for desktop (open panel + explicit Confirm) and single-step for mobile (long-press flow). also include a non-blocking undo toast for 5 minutes. Marco (PM): agree. propose to A/B test two variants: A) Focused Confirm panel (this) vs B) Inline micro-popover confirm (less friction). experiment ids: focused_confirm_v1, inline_popover_v1. metrics: rollback_attempt, rollback_confirmed, rollback_undo_5m, accidental_rollback_rate. Dev (Eng): engineering constraints: inline popover will be cheaper to implement but has higher accidental click risk. focused panel is safer but needs mid-panel lazy fetch of metrics + diff. we'll implement both as feature flags. debounce confirm on server and include idempotency token. Pri (A11y): microcopy tweak: avoid command verbs like "undo" in the confirm label. use explicit text: "You can undo this action within 5 minutes from the toast." Also ensure color isn't the only signal for canary state. add textual badge and aria-live when status updates. Zoe (Design): changed copy accordingly. confirm button text: "Revert and route traffic"; secondary: "Cancel". toast: "Reverted to vX — Undo" with aria-live=\"polite\". added a brief explanation block for partial canary metrics: "This revision was tested on a subset of traffic; metrics may be incomplete." analytics-bot: suggested telemetry schema: event names => ["rollback_intent", "rollback_confirm_safe", "rollback_confirm_immediate", "rollback_undo_within_5m"], props => ["revision_id", "was_canary", "canary_duration_mins", "user_id", "variant_experiment_id"]. Dev (Eng): noted. for large timelines we'll TTL-cache preview payloads and lazy fetch details on panel open. include prefers-reduced-motion checks when animating panel open/close. sample css: .panel { transition: max-height 220ms ease; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .panel { transition: none; } } Pri (A11y): also ensure keyboard focus order is logical: timeline item -> open panel -> Confirm -> Cancel -> close. provide skip link to jump to timeline list for screen reader users. Lucy (Support): one more: include a small diagnostics link in the confirm panel to open full diff + deployment logs in a separate modal, so support can inspect before confirming. that should help reduce support churn. Zoe (Design): added a 'View diagnostics' button that opens a modal (separate fetch). kept the panel compact by default and only expands details on explicit action. pushed new frames to figma. Marco (PM): great. schedule a 15-min sync with Eng + A11y to agree defaults for the rollout. we'll run the A/B for 2 weeks on a subset of orgs. thanks team. :thumbsup:
